records.source: אָ֖ז אָמַ֣ר שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה יְהוָ֣ה אָמַ֔ר לִשְׁכּ֖וֹן בָּעֲרָפֶֽל׃
records.gloss: Then said Solomon, Yahweh said to dwell in the thick darkness.
pieces: Then Solomon said, \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would dwell in thick darkness.

L.1: Then Solomon said, \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said [that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would] dwell in thick darkness.

R.1: Then Solomon said, \q "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would live in a thick, dark cloud.

decisions.choice: the same words as 1 Kings 8:12
decisions.reason: Verses 1-39 retell Solomon's words and prayer at the dedication of the house as 1 Kings 8:12-50 gives them. This verse is word for word the same as 1 Kings 8:12, and it follows at once on the cloud that filled the house (5:13-14). Where the Hebrew of the two books is the same, the wording here is the same; each record notes how Chronicles differs.

decisions.choice: has said to dwell: has said that he would dwell
decisions.reason: The verb "dwell" is an infinitive after "said". It reports what Yahweh had said about himself; "said" can also mean "decided".

decisions.choice: thick darkness: the dark cloud of Yahweh's presence
decisions.reason: At Sinai Moses drew near to "the thick darkness where God was" (Exodus 20:21; Deuteronomy 4:11; 5:22), and Yahweh appeared in the cloud over the ark's cover (Leviticus 16:2). The cloud that has just filled the house (5:13-14) is that darkness: Yahweh is truly present, yet hidden.

decisions.choice: live in a thick, dark cloud (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 8:12: Readable says "live" for "dwell" and describes the thick darkness as a dark cloud, linking it with the cloud of 5:13-14.

records.heading: Solomon speaks to the people

records.source: וַֽאֲנִ֛י בָּנִ֥יתִי בֵית־זְבֻ֖ל לָ֑ךְ וּמָכ֥וֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ֖ עוֹלָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I, I have built a house of loftiness for you, and a place for your dwelling forever.
pieces: I myself have built a lofty house for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q a place for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to dwell forever."

L.2: And I, I have built an exalted house for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q and a place for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} dwelling forever."

R.2: Now I have built a magnificent temple for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q a place where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can live forever."

decisions.choice: And I, I have built: Solomon's own part, set beside Yahweh's word
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 8:13 doubles the verb, "I have surely built". Chronicles instead puts the pronoun "I" first: Yahweh said he would dwell in darkness, and Solomon for his part has built him a house. Chronicles also joins the second line with "and". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: a house of loftiness: an exalted, royal dwelling
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 8:13. The rare word is used of God's "holy and glorious dwelling" in heaven (Isaiah 63:15). In related languages it is a title meaning "prince", so the house is a dwelling fit for a king.

decisions.choice: a place for your dwelling: as Moses sang at the sea
decisions.reason: The same words are used in the Song of the Sea: "the place for your dwelling that you have made, Yahweh, the sanctuary" (Exodus 15:17). Solomon sees the house as the fulfillment of that promise.

decisions.choice: I myself (Balanced); magnificent temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the stress the Hebrew puts on "I". Readable keeps the wording of 1 Kings 8:13 and gives the sense of the rare word with a common one.

records.source: וַיַּסֵּ֤ב הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶת־פָּנָ֔יו וַיְבָ֕רֶךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל־קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכָל־קְהַ֥ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עוֹמֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And turned the king his face and blessed all [the] assembly of Israel, and all [the] assembly of Israel [was] standing.
pieces: Then the king turned around and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood there.

L.3: And the king turned his face around and blessed all the assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel [was] standing.

R.3: Then the king turned around to face all the people of Israel who were gathered there. They were all standing, and he blessed them.

decisions.choice: the same words as 1 Kings 8:14
decisions.reason: This verse is word for word the same as 1 Kings 8:14, and the wording is the same.

decisions.choice: turned his face: from facing the house to facing the people
decisions.reason: Solomon had spoken his words about the house toward the sanctuary (verses 1-2). Now he turns to the people gathered in the courtyard.

decisions.choice: assembly: Israel gathered for worship
decisions.reason: The word is used of Israel called together before Yahweh, as at Sinai (Deuteronomy 9:10; 18:16).

decisions.choice: all the people of Israel who were gathered there (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "assembly" as the people who had gathered.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר בְּפִ֔יו אֵ֖ת דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֑י וּבְיָדָ֥יו מִלֵּ֖א לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And he said, Blessed [be] Yahweh, [the] God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth with David my father, and with his hands has fulfilled, saying,
pieces: He said, "Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, who with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own mouth made a promise to my father David and with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own hands has now fulfilled it. For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said,

L.4: And he said, "Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, who spoke with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth to David my father, and with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands has fulfilled [it], saying,

R.4: He said, "Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel! He made a promise to my father David, and now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised. This is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said:

decisions.choice: with his hands: 1 Kings 8:15 has "hand"
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 1 Kings 8:15 except that Chronicles has the plural "hands". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: blessed be: praised and thanked
decisions.reason: When people bless God, they praise him and give him thanks for what he has done (Genesis 24:27; Exodus 18:10).

decisions.choice: with his mouth ... with his hands: what Yahweh said, he has now done
decisions.reason: The mouth that spoke the promise and the hands that carried it out belong to the same God. Solomon says it again in verse 15.

decisions.choice: spoke to David my father: the promise through Nathan
decisions.reason: Yahweh promised David that his son would build a house for him (1 Chronicles 17:11-12; 2 Samuel 7:12-13).

decisions.choice: Praise (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "Praise" because "bless" said of God is not familiar to many readers.

records.source: מִן־הַיּ֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצֵ֣אתִי אֶת־עַמִּי֮ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ לֹא־בָחַ֣רְתִּֽי בְעִ֗יר מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִבְנ֣וֹת בַּ֔יִת לִהְי֥וֹת שְׁמִ֖י שָׁ֑ם וְלֹא־בָחַ֣רְתִּֽי בְאִ֔ישׁ לִהְי֥וֹת נָגִ֖יד עַל־עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: From the day that I brought out my people from [the] land of Egypt, not I chose a city from all [the] tribes of Israel to build a house for being my name there, and not I chose a man to be ruler over my people Israel.
pieces: 'Ever since the day I brought {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people out of the land of Egypt, I have chosen no city in any tribe of Israel in which to build a house where {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name would be, and I have chosen no man to be ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.

L.5: 'From the day that I brought {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people out of the land of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from all the tribes of Israel to build a house, for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name to be there; and I have not chosen a man to be ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.

R.5: 'I have not chosen any city in all the tribes of Israel as the place to build a temple for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, not since I brought {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people out of the land of Egypt. And I did not choose any man to lead {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.

decisions.choice: a longer text than 1 Kings 8:16
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 8:16 says "out of Egypt" and goes straight on to the choice of David. Chronicles says "out of the land of Egypt" and has two more sayings: Yahweh chose no man as ruler (this verse) and then chose Jerusalem (verse 6). In both books the choice of a place and the choice of a king belong together.

decisions.choice: for my name to be there: a house where Yahweh is known and called on
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy speaks of the place Yahweh would choose "to put his name there" (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11). His name is Yahweh himself as he has made himself known; where his name is, he is present to hear his people (verses 20-21).

decisions.choice: I did not choose a man to be ruler: no lasting choice before David
decisions.reason: Saul had been made king (1 Chronicles 10), but his rule did not last and no city was chosen with him. The lasting choice of a king came with the choice of Jerusalem (verse 6; 1 Chronicles 17:7).

decisions.choice: ruler (Literal, Balanced); lead (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word *nagid* is "ruler" at Literal and Balanced and "leader" at Readable, as in Samuel and Kings. Readable says "house" as "temple", as in 1 Kings 8.

records.source: וָאֶבְחַר֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לִהְי֥וֹת שְׁמִ֖י שָׁ֑ם וָאֶבְחַ֣ר בְּדָוִ֔יד לִהְי֖וֹת עַל־עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And I have chosen in Jerusalem for being my name there, and I have chosen in David to be over my people Israel.
pieces: But I have chosen Jerusalem as the place where {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will be, and I have chosen David to rule over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'

L.6: But I have chosen Jerusalem for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name to be there, and I have chosen David to be over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'

R.6: But now I have chosen Jerusalem as the place for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and I have chosen David to rule over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.'

decisions.choice: I have chosen Jerusalem: not in 1 Kings 8:16
decisions.reason: The choice of Jerusalem is not in the Hebrew of 1 Kings 8:16, which has only "and I chose David". The city and the king are chosen together, as in Psalm 78:68-70 and 132:11-14.

decisions.choice: to be over my people: to rule them
decisions.reason: To be "over" a people is to be their ruler (1 Chronicles 17:7).

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: The "and" that opens the verse sets Yahweh's choice against the long time when he chose no city and no man (verse 5).

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י עִם־לְבַ֖ב דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֑י לִבְנ֣וֹת בַּ֔יִת לְשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And it was with [the] heart of David my father to build a house for [the] name of Yahweh, [the] God of Israel.
pieces: My father David had it in his heart to build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

L.7: And it was with the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

R.7: My father David wanted to build a temple for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: the same words as 1 Kings 8:17
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 1 Kings 8:17, and the wording is the same.

decisions.choice: it was with the heart of David: David intended and longed to do it
decisions.reason: The heart is where plans are made. David told Nathan that he wanted to build a house for the ark (1 Chronicles 17:1-2; 28:2).

decisions.choice: wanted (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the heart idiom in plain words.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֔י יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָיָה֙ עִם־לְבָ֣בְךָ֔ לִבְנ֥וֹת בַּ֖יִת לִשְׁמִ֑י הֱֽטִיב֔וֹתָ כִּ֥י הָיָ֖ה עִם־לְבָבֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to David my father, Because that it was with your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was with your heart.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to my father David, 'You wanted to build a house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and you did well to have this in your heart.

L.8: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to David my father, 'Because it was with your heart to build a house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, you did well that it was with your heart.

R.8: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to my father David, 'You wanted to build a temple for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. It was good that you wanted to do this.

decisions.choice: the same words as 1 Kings 8:18
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 1 Kings 8:18, and the wording is the same.

decisions.choice: you did well: Yahweh approves David's desire though he does not let him carry it out
decisions.reason: These words are not in 1 Chronicles 17 or 2 Samuel 7, though they agree with them: Yahweh honors what David wanted and gives the task to his son.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 8:18: the "and" points to a contrast. David wanted to build, but Yahweh said otherwise.

records.source: רַ֣ק אַתָּ֔ה לֹ֥א תִבְנֶ֖ה הַבָּ֑יִת כִּ֤י בִנְךָ֙ הַיּוֹצֵ֣א מֵֽחֲלָצֶ֔יךָ הֽוּא־יִבְנֶ֥ה הַבַּ֖יִת לִשְׁמִֽי׃
records.gloss: Only you not will build the house, but your son, the one coming out from your loins, he will build the house for my name.
pieces: Yet you are not the one who will build the house. Your son, your own offspring, is the one who will build the house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.'

L.9: Only, you will not build the house; but your son, who will come out of your loins, he will build the house for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.'

R.9: But you will not be the one to build it. Your own son will build the temple for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.'

decisions.choice: the same words as 1 Kings 8:19
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 1 Kings 8:19, except that Kings has a fuller word for "but". The wording is the same.

decisions.choice: who will come out of your loins: your own son
decisions.reason: The loins stand for the body as the source of children (Genesis 35:11). The words echo the promise in 2 Samuel 7:12.

decisions.choice: you will not build the house
decisions.reason: David himself gives the reason in Chronicles: he had shed much blood and fought great wars (1 Chronicles 22:8; 28:3).

decisions.choice: your own offspring (Balanced); your own son (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the picture of the loins in plain words.

records.source: וַיָּ֣קֶם יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־דְּבָר֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר וָאָק֡וּם תַּחַת֩ דָּוִ֨יד אָבִ֜י וָאֵשֵׁ֣ב׀עַל־כִּסֵּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וָאֶבְנֶ֣ה הַבַּ֔יִת לְשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And established Yahweh his word that he spoke, and I have risen in place of David my father, and I sit on [the] throne of Israel as spoke Yahweh, and I have built the house for [the] name of Yahweh, [the] God of Israel.
pieces: Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has kept the promise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made. I have taken the place of my father David and sit on Israel's throne, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised, and I have built this house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

L.10: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has established {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke; and I have risen in place of David my father, and I sit on the throne of Israel, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke; and I have built the house for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

R.10: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has kept {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promise. I have become king after my father David, and I sit on the throne of Israel, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised. And I have built the temple for the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: the same words as 1 Kings 8:20
decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 1 Kings 8:20, and the wording is the same.

decisions.choice: established his word: made his promise stand, kept it
decisions.reason: The verb means "make stand". A word that is made to stand is one that comes true (1 Chronicles 17:23).

decisions.choice: I have risen in place of David: I have become king after him
decisions.reason: To "rise" in someone's place is to succeed him.

decisions.choice: promise; promised (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Word" and "spoke" here mean the promise Yahweh made, so Balanced and Readable say "promise".

records.source: וָאָשִׂ֥ים שָׁם֙ אֶת־הָ֣אָר֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֖ם בְּרִ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרַ֖ת עִם־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And I have put there the ark, where there [is the] covenant of Yahweh that he made with [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: There I have placed the ark, which holds the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}."

L.11: And I have put the ark there, in which [is] the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made with the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel."

R.11: In the temple I have put the ark. Inside the ark is the covenant {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}."

decisions.choice: different words from 1 Kings 8:21
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 8:21 says "I have set there a place for the ark" and that the covenant was made "with our fathers when he brought them out of the land of Egypt". Chronicles says "I have put the ark there" and that the covenant was made "with the sons of Israel". Both speak of the covenant made at Sinai.

decisions.choice: the covenant: the stone tablets on which the covenant was written
decisions.reason: What is in the ark is the two tablets (5:10), called "the tablets of the covenant" (Deuteronomy 9:9). The covenant is named for the tablets that record it.

decisions.choice: children of Israel (Literal); Israelites (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The whole people, men and women, are meant, so the inclusive form is the default, as everywhere.

records.source: וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֗ד לִפְנֵי֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה נֶ֖גֶד כָּל־קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּפְרֹ֖שׂ כַּפָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he stood before [the] altar of Yahweh in front of all [the] assembly of Israel, and spread out his palms.
pieces: Then Solomon took his place before the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in front of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands.

L.12: And he stood before the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in front of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his palms.

R.12: Then Solomon stood in front of the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with all the people of Israel there. He held up his open hands to pray.

decisions.choice: 1 Kings 8:22 names Solomon and ends "toward the heavens"
decisions.reason: Here the verb has no named subject, and the words "toward the heavens" are held back to the end of verse 13. Chronicles stops to describe the platform Solomon stood on, then repeats "spread out his palms" to take up the story again.

decisions.choice: spread out his palms: the posture of prayer
decisions.reason: People prayed standing or kneeling with open hands lifted up (Exodus 9:29; Isaiah 1:15).

decisions.choice: the altar of Yahweh: the great bronze altar in the courtyard
decisions.reason: This is the bronze altar for burnt offerings that Solomon made (4:1), standing in front of the house (7:7).

decisions.choice: Solomon; to pray (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Solomon, since the verse says only "he". Readable says what the gesture meant, since the prayer follows.

records.source: כִּֽי־עָשָׂ֨ה שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה כִּיּ֣וֹר נְחֹ֗שֶׁת וַֽיִּתְּנֵהוּ֮ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעֲזָרָה֒ חָמֵ֨שׁ אַמּ֜וֹת אָרְכּ֗וֹ וְחָמֵ֤שׁ אַמּוֹת֙ רָחְבּ֔וֹ וְאַמּ֥וֹת שָׁל֖וֹשׁ קוֹמָת֑וֹ וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד עָלָ֗יו וַיִּבְרַ֤ךְ עַל־בִּרְכָּיו֙ נֶ֚גֶד כָּל־קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּפְרֹ֥שׂ כַּפָּ֖יו הַשָּׁמָֽיְמָה׃
records.gloss: For had made Solomon a platform of bronze and had put it in [the] middle of the court, five cubits its length and five cubits its width and cubits three its height, and he stood on it and knelt on his knees in front of all [the] assembly of Israel and spread out his palms toward the heavens.
pieces: Solomon had made a bronze platform, {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} long, {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} wide and {{units:about 4 1/2 feet|three cubits}} high, and had set it in the middle of the courtyard. He stood on it, then knelt down in front of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands toward heaven.

L.13: For Solomon had made a bronze platform and had put it in the middle of the court, five cubits its length, and five cubits its width, and three cubits its height; and he stood on it, and knelt on his knees in front of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his palms toward the heavens.

R.13: Solomon had made a bronze platform and put it in the middle of the courtyard. It was {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} long, {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|five cubits}} wide and {{units:about 4 1/2 feet|three cubits}} high. He stood on it. Then he knelt down in front of all the people of Israel and held up his hands toward heaven.

decisions.choice: the bronze platform: not in 1 Kings 8
decisions.reason: Kings has no account of the platform. It says only, at the end of the prayer, that Solomon rose from kneeling before the altar (1 Kings 8:54). Chronicles explains where he stood and knelt so that the whole assembly could see him.

decisions.choice: platform: a raised stand
decisions.reason: The word usually means a basin, like the bronze basins for washing (4:6). Here it is something Solomon stood on, so it is a raised stand, perhaps shaped like a large bowl.

decisions.choice: the court: the great courtyard where the people stood
decisions.reason: The house had the court of the priests and the great court (4:9). The platform stood in the middle of the courtyard, among the people.

decisions.choice: For: the verse explains verse 12
decisions.reason: The verse looks back to explain how Solomon could pray in front of the whole assembly, then repeats "spread out his palms" to return to the moment of prayer.

decisions.choice: about 7 1/2 feet; about 4 1/2 feet (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: A cubit is about 18 inches, so five cubits is about 7 1/2 feet and three cubits about 4 1/2 feet. Literal keeps the cubit; Balanced and Readable give the modern measure with the cubit as the alternative.

decisions.choice: For left out (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable tell the explanation as a new sentence, so the word "for" is not needed.

decisions.choice: 1 Kings 8:23 adds "above" and "beneath"
decisions.reason: Kings says "in the heavens above and on the earth beneath". Chronicles has the shorter "in the heavens and on the earth". The rest of the verse is the same, and the wording is the same.

decisions.choice: there is no God like you: Yahweh has no equal
decisions.reason: Israel confessed that no god could be compared with Yahweh, in heaven or on earth (Exodus 15:11; Deuteronomy 4:39).

decisions.choice: keeping the covenant and the steadfast love: faithful to the covenant and to the love it promises
decisions.reason: The same words describe Yahweh in Deuteronomy 7:9, 12. The word for steadfast love (*chesed*) is the loyal, generous love that keeps its commitments. The two nouns belong together: Yahweh keeps his covenant by showing steadfast love.

decisions.choice: walk before you: live in your sight, serving you
decisions.reason: To walk before Yahweh is to live one's whole life aware of him and obeying him (Genesis 17:1).

decisions.choice: steadfast love, slaves (Literal); faithful love, servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: *Chesed* is "steadfast love" at Literal and "faithful love" at Balanced and Readable, as everywhere. Those who serve God are his "slaves" at Literal and "servants" at the other levels, following the rule for *'eved*.

decisions.choice: Solomon prayed (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker and says that what follows is a prayer, after the words to the people in verses 4-11.

decisions.choice: to walk in my law: 1 Kings 8:25 has "to walk before me"
decisions.reason: Kings has "to walk before me as you have walked before me". Chronicles says "to walk in my law": walking before Yahweh means living by his written instruction. The rest of the verse is the same, and the wording is the same.

decisions.choice: a man will not be cut off for you: you will never lack a descendant on the throne
decisions.reason: The promise goes back to 1 Chronicles 17:11-14 and 2 Samuel 7:12-16. Yahweh repeats it to Solomon in 7:18.

decisions.choice: only if: the promise is joined to a condition
decisions.reason: Yahweh's promise to David stands, but each king's place on the throne depends on keeping Yahweh's law.

decisions.choice: my law: Yahweh's instruction
decisions.reason: The word *torah* means teaching or instruction, the whole of what Yahweh taught his people through Moses.

decisions.choice: slave, sons (Literal); servant, descendants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 14 for "slave". "Sons" here means all of David's line, so Balanced and Readable say "descendants".

pieces: But will God really live on earth with human beings? Heaven itself, even the highest heaven, cannot contain {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. How much less this house that I have built!

L.18: But will God truly dwell with humankind on the earth? Look, the heavens and the heavens of the heavens cannot contain {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; how much less this house that I have built!

R.18: But can God really live on earth with people? Even the sky and the highest heaven cannot hold {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. So this temple I have built certainly cannot hold {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!

decisions.choice: with humankind: not in 1 Kings 8:27
decisions.reason: Kings asks "will God truly dwell on the earth?" Chronicles adds "with humankind". Otherwise the verse is the same, and the wording is the same.

decisions.choice: God is not confined to the house
decisions.reason: Solomon has just said that he built a place for Yahweh to dwell forever (verse 2). Now he says that no place can contain him. The house is where Yahweh puts his name and hears prayer (verses 20-21), while he himself dwells in heaven (2:5).

decisions.choice: the heavens of the heavens: the highest heaven
decisions.reason: This is a superlative, like "holy of holies", as in Deuteronomy 10:14.

decisions.choice: certainly cannot hold you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable completes the comparison "how much less" in plain words.

decisions.choice: 1 Kings 8:28 adds "today"
decisions.reason: Kings ends "is praying before you today". Chronicles leaves out "today". Otherwise the verse is the same, and the wording is the same.

decisions.choice: prayer, plea, cry: three words for asking God
decisions.reason: The first is the general word for prayer. The second is a plea for favor or mercy. The third (*rinnah*) is a loud cry, often of joy, here of urgent asking.

decisions.choice: turn to: give attention to
decisions.reason: To turn toward a prayer is to take notice of it and respond (Psalm 102:18).

decisions.choice: your servant (all levels); me, I (Readable)
decisions.reason: Solomon speaks of himself politely as "your servant". The words stay "your servant" at every level, as in 1 Kings 8:28; Readable also says "me" and "I" so that it is clear Solomon means himself.

decisions.choice: small differences from 1 Kings 8:29
decisions.reason: Kings says "night and day" and quotes Yahweh directly: "My name shall be there". Chronicles says "day and night" and "where you said you would put your name", the words of Deuteronomy 12:5. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: your eyes open: watching over it with care
decisions.reason: Yahweh's eyes are on the land he cares for (Deuteronomy 11:12), and here on the house and those who pray there.

decisions.choice: toward this place: praying while facing the house, even from far away
decisions.reason: The prayer expects people to pray toward the house when they cannot come to it (verses 26, 29, 34, 38). Daniel prayed in Babylon with his windows open toward Jerusalem (Daniel 6:11).

decisions.choice: your servant (all levels); I (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

decisions.reason: Kings says "hear to the place of your dwelling, to the heavens", and "plea" in the singular. Chronicles says "from" and "pleas". Otherwise the verse is the same.

decisions.choice: hear from heaven: the refrain of the prayer
decisions.reason: The refrain of the prayer comes back in verses 21, 23, 25, 27, 30, 33, 35 and 39. In 1 Kings 8 it is "hear [in] the heavens"; Chronicles nearly always says "hear from the heavens". The house is the place toward which prayer is made; heaven is where Yahweh dwells and from where he answers.

decisions.choice: forgive: pardon and restore
decisions.reason: In the Bible this verb always has God as its subject. Forgiveness is the main thing Solomon asks for in the cases that follow.

decisions.choice: hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and forgive
decisions.reason: The refrain keeps one wording at each level, as in 1 Kings 8: Literal "hear from the heavens, the place of your dwelling", Balanced "hear from heaven, your dwelling place", Readable "listen from heaven, where you live".

decisions.choice: your servant (all levels); I (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 19.

L.22: If a man sins against his neighbor, and he lays an oath on him to make him swear, and the oath comes before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altar in this house,

R.22: Suppose someone is accused of wronging a neighbor and is made to swear an oath that he is innocent. If he comes and takes this oath in front of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} altar in this temple,

decisions.choice: If: 1 Kings 8:31 has a different opening word
decisions.reason: Kings opens with a word meaning "in the case that", Chronicles with "if". The meaning is the same, and the wording is the same.

decisions.choice: an oath to make him swear: an oath calling down a curse on himself if he is guilty
decisions.reason: When a wrong could not be proved by witnesses, the accused person swore before Yahweh that he was innocent, accepting a curse if he lied (Exodus 22:6-10; Numbers 5:19-22). Yahweh himself was then left to judge.

decisions.choice: he lays an oath on him: the one wronged, or the judges, require the oath
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name who lays the oath on the accused. It is probably the neighbor who brings the charge, or the judges who hear the case.

decisions.choice: accused of; that he is innocent (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the situation: the wrong has not been proved, and the oath is a claim of innocence that only God can test.

R.23: then listen from heaven and act. Judge between {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants. Punish the guilty one for what he has done, and show that the innocent one is right by rewarding him for his righteousness.

decisions.reason: These are words of the law court. A judge was to declare the innocent in the right and the guilty in the wrong (Deuteronomy 25:1). Solomon asks Yahweh to do this where human judges cannot know the truth.

decisions.reason: As in verse 21: the refrain keeps one wording at each level.

decisions.choice: confess (Literal); acknowledge (Balanced); honor (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps one word for this verb through the prayer (verses 24 and 26), as in 1 Kings 8. Readable says "turn back to you", since the turning is toward Yahweh.

decisions.reason: The verse is the same as 1 Kings 8:35 apart from the form of one verb, and the wording is the same.

decisions.choice: the heavens shut up: drought sent as a warning
decisions.reason: The covenant warned that Yahweh would shut up the heavens so that there would be no rain if Israel turned to other gods (Deuteronomy 11:17; Leviticus 26:19). Yahweh answers this request in 7:13-14.

decisions.choice: because you afflict them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels give "because you afflict them": the drought has humbled them and made them turn. The same letters can be read "when you answer them", meaning that they turn from sin when Yahweh answers their prayer. The traditional reading is followed, as in 1 Kings 8:35.

decisions.choice: the people (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names who has sinned, since the verse does not.

decisions.choice: hear the heavens: here, as in 1 Kings 8:36, without "from"
decisions.reason: This is the one place in the refrain where Chronicles, like Kings, has no word for "from": "hear [in] the heavens". The verse is the same as 1 Kings 8:36, and the wording is the same.

decisions.choice: when you teach them: forgiveness goes with Yahweh's teaching
decisions.reason: The little word can mean "when", "for" or "so that". Yahweh forgives as he teaches his people, through the hardship and through his word, the way they should live. The verb "teach" is related to the word *torah*, "instruction".

decisions.choice: your land ... as an inheritance: Yahweh's land given to Israel
decisions.reason: The land belongs to Yahweh (Leviticus 25:23), and he gave it to Israel as a family inheritance. So the rain on it is his gift too (Deuteronomy 11:11-14).

decisions.choice: hear [in] the heavens (Literal); hear in heaven (Balanced); slaves, servants
decisions.reason: Where the Hebrew has no "from", Literal and Balanced keep the wording of 1 Kings 8:36; Readable keeps its refrain. "Slaves" at Literal and "servants" at the other levels, as in verse 14; Balanced and Readable take "your servants and your people Israel" as two names for the same people.

decisions.choice: small differences from 1 Kings 8:37
decisions.reason: Chronicles has "and" between the pairs, and "its enemies" in the plural where Kings has "its enemy". The words "in the land of its gates" are the same in both.

decisions.choice: blight, mildew: diseases of the grain
decisions.reason: The first word is the scorching of crops by the hot east wind; the second is a disease that turns grain pale or yellow. They appear together among the covenant curses (Deuteronomy 28:22; Amos 4:9).

decisions.choice: locust, grasshopper: two kinds or stages of locust
decisions.reason: Several Hebrew words name locusts. The second comes from a verb meaning "consume" and may be a stage of the locust's growth, or another insect that strips the fields.

decisions.choice: in the land of their gates: in their cities
decisions.reason: "Gates" stands for cities, as often (Deuteronomy 12:15). The sense is that an enemy besieges one of Israel's towns. The Hebrew speaks of the nation as "it", one body.

decisions.choice: crops are ruined by hot winds (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable describes the blight by its cause, as in 1 Kings 8:37.

decisions.reason: Kings speaks of each one knowing "the plague of his own heart". Chronicles names two things: "his plague and his pain". Both mean the trouble each person feels for himself. Otherwise the verse is the same.

decisions.choice: plague, pain: the disaster and the grief it brings
decisions.reason: The word "plague" picks up the list of verse 28; "pain" is the sorrow and suffering it causes. Each one knows their own trouble and brings it to God.

decisions.choice: by any person or by all your people: one person or the whole nation
decisions.reason: Solomon asks Yahweh to hear both the prayer of one person and the prayer of all Israel together.

decisions.choice: spreading out his palms: praying
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

decisions.choice: their (inclusive); his (traditional)
decisions.reason: "Each" means every person, man or woman, so the pronoun is inclusive by default.

decisions.reason: Kings says "hear [in] the heavens", "forgive and act", and "the heart of all the children of humankind". Chronicles says "from the heavens", has only "forgive" before "give", and has no "all" before "children". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: you alone know the heart of all people
decisions.reason: Only Yahweh sees what is in the heart (1 Samuel 16:7; 1 Chronicles 28:9; Jeremiah 17:10). So only he can forgive and judge rightly.

decisions.choice: the place of your dwelling: heaven, Yahweh's fixed dwelling
decisions.reason: The word for "place" is the one used in verse 2 for the house as "a place for your dwelling". Now Solomon gives the same name to heaven: the house is where prayer is directed, heaven is where Yahweh truly dwells. Verses 33 and 39 use the same words.

decisions.choice: hear from heaven and forgive

decisions.choice: their; children of humankind (inclusive); his; sons of man (traditional)
decisions.reason: Solomon speaks of every human being, so the inclusive form is the default.

When foreigners come and pray toward this temple,

decisions.choice: one verse for 1 Kings 8:41-42
decisions.reason: Kings says the foreigner comes "for the sake of your name", then explains: "for they will hear of your great name and your strong hand and your outstretched arm". Chronicles joins it all in one phrase: he comes "for the sake of your great name and your strong hand and your outstretched arm".

decisions.choice: the foreigner: a person from another nation
decisions.reason: This word means someone who belongs to another people, not the outsider who lives among Israel. Solomon prays for those who come from far away.

decisions.choice: strong hand and outstretched arm: Yahweh's power shown in the exodus
decisions.reason: The pair is used of Yahweh's acts in bringing Israel out of Egypt (Deuteronomy 4:34; 5:15). The nations hear of these acts, as Rahab had (Joshua 2:10).

decisions.choice: they come and pray: the one foreigner stands for many
decisions.reason: The verbs change from singular to plural: Solomon has in mind all the foreigners who will come.

decisions.choice: how great you are; foreigners (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "your great name" as Yahweh's greatness, and follows the plural verbs with "foreigners".

decisions.choice: your name is called over this house: the house belongs to Yahweh
decisions.reason: To have someone's name called over a thing means that it is his (Deuteronomy 28:10; Jeremiah 7:10-11).

decisions.choice: all the peoples of the earth: Yahweh's purpose reaches beyond Israel
decisions.reason: Yahweh promised that all the families of the earth would be blessed through Abraham (Genesis 12:3). Later the house is called "a house of prayer for all peoples" (Isaiah 56:7).

decisions.reason: As in verse 30.

decisions.choice: know who you are; respect and obey; belongs to you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains what it means to know Yahweh's name and to have his name called over the house, and words the fear of God as in verse 31.

decisions.choice: by the way that you send them: a war Yahweh has sent them to fight
decisions.reason: Solomon speaks of battles Yahweh has commanded, not wars of Israel's own choosing.

decisions.choice: toward this city: facing Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Soldiers far away would turn toward Jerusalem and its house to pray (verse 20).

pieces: When they sin against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} (and there is no one who never sins), and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are angry with them and hand them over to an enemy, and their captors take them away as prisoners to a land far away or near,

L.36: When they sin against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} (for there is no human who does not sin), and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are angry with them and give them over before an enemy, and their captors take them captive to a land far or near,

R.36: Everyone sins. So suppose {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people sin against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} become angry with them and let an enemy defeat them. Suppose their captors take them away as prisoners to a land far away or near.

decisions.choice: to a land far or near: 1 Kings 8:46 has "to the land of the enemy"
decisions.reason: Kings says "to the land of the enemy, far or near"; Chronicles says only "to a land far or near". Otherwise the verse is the same, and the wording is the same.

decisions.choice: there is no one who does not sin
decisions.reason: Solomon admits that sin is universal, his own people included (Ecclesiastes 7:20; Psalm 143:2). The prayer does not hope that Israel will never sin, but that Yahweh will forgive when they turn back.

decisions.choice: taken captive to a distant land: the exile the covenant warned of
decisions.reason: The law warned that unfaithful Israel would be scattered among the nations (Leviticus 26:33-39; Deuteronomy 28:36, 64). Chronicles ends with Judah carried off to Babylon and then allowed to return (36:20-23), so its first readers would hear their own story in these verses.

decisions.choice: Everyone sins (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable moves the remark in brackets to the front as a short sentence of its own, and names "your people" as the subject.

decisions.choice: the land of their captivity: 1 Kings 8:47 has "the land of their captors"
decisions.reason: The two words look and sound alike in Hebrew. Chronicles also joins the three verbs of the confession a little differently. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: bring back to their heart: come to their senses, take it to heart
decisions.reason: The phrase means to think again and see things as they are (Deuteronomy 4:39; 30:1).

decisions.choice: bring back ... taken captive ... turn back: a play on sounds
decisions.reason: "Turn back" and "take captive" sound alike in Hebrew. Those who were taken captive (*nishbu*) now turn back (*shavu*) to Yahweh in the land of their captivity.

decisions.choice: We have sinned, we have done wrong and acted wickedly
decisions.reason: The three verbs make a full confession. Later generations used the same words (Psalm 106:6; Daniel 9:5).

decisions.reason: Kings says "in the land of their enemies who took them captive" and "they pray to you toward their land". Chronicles says "in the land of their captivity where they took them captive" and "they pray toward their land". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: return to you with all their heart and all their soul
decisions.reason: Moses promised that if Israel in exile returned to Yahweh with all their heart and soul, he would have mercy and gather them again (Deuteronomy 4:29-31; 30:1-3).

decisions.choice: pray toward their land, the city and the house
decisions.reason: Exiles far from home would pray facing Jerusalem, as Daniel did (Daniel 6:11). The three goals, land, city and house, narrow down to the place where Yahweh's name is.

decisions.choice: where they took them captive: the captors are not named
decisions.reason: "They" here are those who carried Israel off, as the context shows.

decisions.choice: where they were carried off (Balanced); where they were taken as captives (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the unnamed "they" into a passive, so that it is not mistaken for Israel.

decisions.choice: a different ending from 1 Kings 8:51-53
decisions.reason: Kings ends with Israel as Yahweh's people brought out of Egypt and asks that his eyes be open to their pleas (1 Kings 8:51-53). Chronicles asks that his eyes be open and his ears attentive to prayer in this place, and Yahweh answers with these very words in 7:15. The words "let your ears be attentive" are also in Psalm 130:2 and Nehemiah 1:6, 11.

decisions.choice: the prayer of this place: prayer made in it or toward it
decisions.reason: The phrase is short for every prayer that is prayed at the house or toward it (verses 20-39).

decisions.choice: eyes open and ears attentive: watching and listening with care
decisions.reason: Yahweh's open eyes and listening ears mean that he notices and answers (verse 20).

decisions.choice: the prayer that is prayed in this place (Balanced); every prayer made in this place (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the prayer of this place" means. Readable puts "attentive ears" as listening carefully.

decisions.choice: Psalm 132:8-9 with differences
decisions.reason: Solomon ends his prayer with words found in Psalm 132:8-9. Chronicles adds "And now" and "God" after Yahweh's name (twice), and uses a shorter word for "resting place". The Psalm asks that the priests be clothed with "righteousness" and that the faithful "shout for joy"; here they are to be clothed with "salvation", as Yahweh promises in Psalm 132:16, and to "rejoice in what is good". Where the words are the same, the wording is the same as in Psalm 132.

decisions.choice: Arise, Yahweh, to your resting place: the ark comes to rest
decisions.reason: "Arise, Yahweh" was said when the ark set out in the wilderness (Numbers 10:35). Now the ark has been brought into the house (5:7), its lasting home; David had planned "a house of rest for the ark" (1 Chronicles 28:2).

decisions.choice: the ark of your strength: the sign of your power
decisions.reason: The ark went before Israel in battle and showed Yahweh's power (Psalm 78:61; 1 Samuel 4-6).

decisions.choice: clothed with salvation: marked by Yahweh's help
decisions.reason: Being clothed with a quality means it covers the person and can be seen (Isaiah 61:10). The priests are to show the salvation, the rescue and well-being, that Yahweh gives.

decisions.choice: faithful ones; the good
decisions.reason: The faithful (*chasidim*) are those loyal to Yahweh and his covenant; the word comes from *chesed*, loyal love. "The good" is the good that Yahweh gives his people, their blessing and well-being (Nehemiah 9:25, 35).

decisions.choice: Arise (Literal); Rise up (Balanced); Get up (Readable); LORD God
decisions.reason: As in Psalm 132:8. The divine name is called on directly, so it has no "the" before it, as in the Psalm.

decisions.choice: the good things you give them (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says where the good comes from, as the Psalm's promise does (Psalm 132:15-16).

L.42: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God, do not turn away the face of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed; \q remember the acts of steadfast love of David {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave."

R.42: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God, do not turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} back on the kings {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have anointed. \q Remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant David."

decisions.choice: Psalm 132:10 with differences
decisions.reason: The Psalm reads: "For the sake of David your servant, do not turn away the face of your anointed." Chronicles adds "Yahweh God", puts the request about the anointed first, and in place of "for the sake of David" asks Yahweh to "remember the steadfast love of David". The same words, "the steadfast love of David", stand in Isaiah 55:3.

decisions.choice: your anointed ones (plural)
decisions.reason: The Leningrad text has the plural, "your anointed ones": the kings of David's line, Solomon and those after him. Many Hebrew manuscripts, the Greek translation, and Psalm 132:10 have the singular, "your anointed", meaning the reigning king, here Solomon himself. The difference is one letter. The meaning is close: in both, the king of David's line asks not to be refused.

decisions.choice: turn away the face: refuse a request
decisions.reason: To turn away someone's face is to send them away with their request refused (1 Kings 2:16-20).

decisions.choice: the steadfast love of David: love shown to David
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean the steadfast love Yahweh showed and promised to David, his lasting promise of a king on the throne (1 Chronicles 17:13; Psalm 89:2-5, 50; Isaiah 55:3). It can also mean David's own loyal deeds for Yahweh, as Chronicles uses the plural of this word for the good deeds of Hezekiah and Josiah (32:32; 35:26). Since the prayer has asked Yahweh to keep his promise to David (verses 15-17), the first sense is taken.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (plural): acts of loyal love
decisions.reason: *Chesed* is the loyal, generous love that keeps its commitments. The plural speaks of its many acts or promises.

decisions.choice: acts of steadfast love, slave (Literal); faithful love, servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: *Chesed* is "steadfast love" at Literal and "faithful love" at Balanced and Readable, as in verse 14; Literal shows the plural with "acts of" and keeps the phrase open to both readings. "Your servant" follows the rule for *'eved* as in verses 15-17, so Literal has "slave" here, where Psalm 132:10 has "servant" at every level.

decisions.choice: the kings you have anointed (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the anointed are, as Psalm 132:10 does for the singular.
